Job Description

We are looking for a skilled Bubble.io developer to build a secure, mobile-first web app for our clients. The application will be accessed primarily on smartphones via physical QR code scans on magnets.

We have a complete, interactive Figma prototype ready to review. Your job will be translating this design into a fully functioning, responsive Bubble app with database privacy controls and automated real-time data exports.

Design Reference

Figma Interactive Prototype: https://www.figma.com/make/5mcLRrfdVs1NbBNWdWsRrJ/Client-Access-QR-Code?fullscreen=1&t=k7rL9ejxsFGY4J5a-1&code-node-id=0-6

**Front-end UI build in Bubble.io must visually match the layouts, colors, and button placements established in the Figma design across mobile Safari and Chrome.**

Core User Workflows & App Architecture

1. Passcode Gate & Security:
* User lands on the app via QR scan containing a secret URL parameter.
* SEO blocking (`noindex` & `robots.txt`) configured to keep the app hidden from search engines.
* Client logs in by entering a **4-letter passcode** (the first 4 letters of their street address).
* Verified against a client database table before unlocking the main dashboard.

2. Main Menu (4 Action Buttons):
Button 1: Order / Refill Prescription
Button 2: Request Documents
Button 3: Instructions, How-to, Procedures (Secondary menu displaying viewable/(non-downloadable) PDF documents).
Button 4: Clinical After Hours Support - Form submission "Tap to Call" phone link if field are filled out and recorded in .csv

3. Data Pipeline (Google Sheets / CSV Sync):
All form submissions across Prescription Refills, Document Requests, and After-Hours Support must automatically update a live **Google Sheet** (or generate an exportable CSV dataset via Bubble Backend Workflows) in real time or hourly.

Developer Responsibilities

Translate provided Figma layouts into responsive Bubble pages using the modern Flexbox engine.

Set up database architecture, relationships, and strict Data Privacy Rules Privacy to prevent unauthorized web scraping/browser inspection.

Implement address passcode authentication logic and telephone protocols.

Set up real-time Google Sheets / CSV sync via plugins or scheduled backend workflows.

Conduct end-to-end testing across mobile iOS Safari and Android Chrome.

---

Project Structure & Payment

This project will be managed via Fixed-Price Milestones:
1. **Milestone 1:** Database Architecture, Passcode Auth & Security/SEO Lockdown (Database Architecture, Security & Authentication, setup database schema & client tables, build address passcode authentication logic, configure noindex SEO shielding & Data Privacy Rules)
-25% of budget allocation

2. **Milestone 2:** Responsive UI Build (Figma Implementation) & Navigation (Translate Figma wireframe screens into Bubble. build Passcode Gate, 4-Button Main Menu, PDF viewer, & submenus. Mobile responsive layout testing (iOS & Android).
-25% of budget allocation

3. **Milestone 3:** Form Workflows, Google Sheets / CSV Data Pipeline & Click-to-Call (Forms, Real-Time Data Pipeline & Call Triggers, Build input forms for Prescription Refills, Documents, & After-Hours, Configure real-time Google Sheets / CSV backend sync, Set up "Tap to Call" phone action for after-hours care.)
-25% budget allocation

4. **Milestone 4:** Mobile QA Testing, Bug Fixes & App Transfer
-25% budget allocation

Total Project Fixed Price: $1000.00 (CAD)
Client's questions:
  • Have you reviewed our Figma prototype? What specific Bubble.io features or plugins will you use to recreate the core workflows shown in the design?
  • How will you ensure the app's responsiveness matches the exact layout across different mobile screen sizes?

About Us
The Harbors Video Project (THVP) opens a window on the underwater world through exploration, research, and education. With over 3,500 hours of recorded video and 5,000+ species observations mapped across our local waters, we are building an interactive "Explore" platform. Our goal is to make the life beneath our coastal waters visible and understandable to the people who live, play, and work near them.


The Role
We are looking for a creative, science-minded Social Media Coordinator to help us drive traffic to our interactive website and engage a growing community of ocean lovers, divers, and educators. In this phase, you will not just be posting pictures; you will be turning our massive video library of raw underwater footage and associated observation data into social media content that encourages people to visit, explore, and provide feedback on our digital platform as well as partner with us for educational, scientific or conservation purposes. We are looking for someone who will bring ideas, test them, and learn from what works.

We are looking for someone part-time who can spend around 10 hours/week to get us started. Down the line, this could grow into more. Early success will be measured primarily by whether the content gets people exploring the site, interacting with THVP, providing useful feedback, and returning - not simply by follower counts.


Key Responsibilities
Short-Form Video Optimization: Edit and optimize raw underwater clips into compelling social media videos.

Interactive Content Creation: Craft engaging captions and interactive stories that encourage users to visit our Explore site to research the local waters or learn more, or to partner with us.

Audience Engagement & Feedback: Manage our social feeds, respond to comments, spark conversations about marine biology and exploration, and actively prompt followers for feedback on our website's user experience.

Testing & Learning: Track which content and calls to action actually drive visits to Explore, interaction, feedback, and return engagement, and use those results to refine the content mix.

Channel Management: Schedule and publish content 2–3 times per week across our priority social media channels, using a focused initial mix that fits the available 10 hours/week.


Qualifications & Experience
Background in Marine Science: A degree, relevant coursework, professional experience, or demonstrated strong foundational knowledge in Marine Biology, Environmental Science, Oceanography, or a closely related field. You must be able to write scientifically accurate, educational captions.

Video Editing Workflow: Experience editing engaging, fast-paced social media video.

Time Management: Proven ability to work independently, prioritize effectively within an initial 10-hour weekly budget, and use efficient workflows and templates.

Software Experience Bonus: Experience with DaVinci Resolve is beneficial, as we are planning on standardizing on this for remote video production. An understanding of basic color correction for underwater footage is a major plus.

How to Apply
In your message, please look at our interactive website (https://explore.theharborsvideoproject.org) and pitch us one or two creative ideas on how you would use our existing video library and data to actively engage people and get them exploring the platform. Briefly explain why you think the ideas would work and what you would look at to judge whether they are driving meaningful engagement. Also tell us which platforms you would prioritize first and why.

IMPORTANT: Please apply only if you are genuinely capable of managing the entire project described below from beginning to end. I am not looking for professionals to handle individual parts of the work. I need one person capable of taking ownership of and coordinating the complete development. If you do not have the skills and experience required to cover all the areas described below, please do not apply.

I am looking for an experienced Product Development / Mechanical Design Engineer with strong DFM and industrialization skills who can take an existing physical product and bring it from prototype stage to a genuinely manufacturable small-series product.

I am NOT looking for a purely theoretical designer. I need someone practical, adaptable and solution-oriented — someone who does not simply identify problems, but proposes realistic, cost-effective and manufacturable solutions.

The product is already developed: I have a physical prototype, CAD/3D models, electronics, firmware and the mechanical structure. You will NOT be starting from zero.

The project has three main areas:

1. PLASTIC PARTS / DFM OPTIMIZATION

Some current components are manufactured using 3D printing and CNC/router machining. I want to preserve the existing industrial design while redesigning the main parts for faster and more cost-effective production.

Main components:
- central console → ideally 2 molded shells, upper/lower;
- hanger → ideally 2 molded shells, front/rear;
- base cover → one component or an extremely simple assembly.

The engineer should evaluate the most suitable manufacturing process (thermoforming, vacuum casting, molding or other solutions), considering initial production batches of approximately 20–40 units and low tooling investment.

2. SANITIZING / FRAGRANCE UPGRADE MODULE

The base product already uses forced airflow, hot/cold air, automatic cycles, electronics and app control.

I want to develop an additional compact module for sanitizing/deodorizing and fragrance using atomization/nebulization or another effective solution.

It must be modular: the same platform should be available as a base version or with the upgrade module, ideally allowing the upgrade to be installed later as well.

3. CUSTOM PACKAGING

Design a professional custom packaging solution, ideally a carrying case with internal protection, suitable for transporting the disassembled product and economically manufacturable in relatively small initial quantities.

FINAL OBJECTIVE

I do not want only renders or theoretical concepts. At the end of the project I want a complete package that can actually be used to move into production:
- final CAD/STEP files;
- DFM-ready parts;
- BOM and technical specifications;
- files required for prototyping and manufacturing;
- clear manufacturing process recommendations;
- ideally identification and contact details of real manufacturers/suppliers for plastic molding and custom packaging.

I am open to manufacturers in Asia or other regions where good quality can be achieved while keeping tooling and production costs low.

I own a 3D printer, so during development I can quickly prototype parts, brackets and design modifications myself. This allows us to work iteratively: design → print → test → modify, without outsourcing every prototype.

I am looking for ONE PERSON capable of managing and coordinating the complete development.

KEY REQUIREMENTS

- proven mechanical/product development experience;
- strong DFM and plastic manufacturing knowledge;
- ability to design around real manufacturing costs;
- mechanical/electronic integration capability;
- ability to identify or evaluate manufacturers and suppliers;
- practical and solution-oriented mindset;
- consistent and reliable communication;
- ability to respect deadlines.

CONFIDENTIALITY

An NDA is attached and must be signed before the complete technical material is shared.

Confidentiality is extremely important to me. CAD files, images, technical information and any details regarding the product must not be disclosed, shared or used outside this project.

BUDGET & LONG-TERM COLLABORATION

My budget is currently limited because I have already invested significantly in developing the prototype. I am therefore looking for a professional with realistic and accessible pricing who knows how to achieve concrete results using the available resources efficiently.

I am not looking for beginners or recent graduates. This is a real and already advanced product, so I will consider candidates with solid, demonstrable experience.

I do not necessarily see this as a one-off project. If I find someone capable, consistent and reliable, with whom I work well, I would be very interested in continuing the collaboration long-term and growing together as the business and future products develop.

TIMELINE: approximately 1 month. I would like this development phase completed by November.

When applying, please briefly provide:
- confirmation that you understand the complete scope and can personally manage the entire project;
- your experience taking physical prototypes into production;
- how you would approach the work;
- realistic timeline;
- preferably a fixed-price proposal.

I am looking for someone who can genuinely take ownership of the project and turn it into something that can actually be manufactured while preserving the design, low production costs and original objectives.

We are a Romanian digital marketing agency looking for a long-term tracking partner to work with us as a subcontractor, behind the scenes. This first project is for one of our clients, a Romanian eCommerce business, running on Shopify.

The situation
Server-side tracking and GA4 are currently managed by another vendor. A recent audit surfaced data quality problems, so the client is moving these two areas to a new partner. We take over in Q4 2026, with go-live on 1 January 2027. Assume you will receive little or no documentation from the previous vendor.

Current stack
Shopify, GA4 with BigQuery export, Google Tag Manager (web container), a server-side GTM container on a vendor-managed first-party subdomain, Google Ads, TikTok pixel, Klaviyo, Microsoft Clarity, plus a consent layer.

Scope 1, server-side tracking
Audit the existing server-side container and GTM setup. Fix what the audit finds. Document the full architecture (tags, triggers, variables, data flows) so the client owns it. Test and validate every change before it touches production. Monitor data integrity after go-live.

Scope 2, GA4 audit
Full audit of the GA4 configuration: events, conversions, custom parameters, acquisition source/medium, BigQuery integration. Reconcile GA4 against BigQuery and fix the causes of any discrepancy. Deliver a prioritised remediation plan. Report on data quality on an agreed cadence.

Acceptance criteria the client set
Zero critical errors in server-side validation. Zero duplicate transactions. Source/medium attributed for at least 99% of traffic. experiment_id and variant_id present on all relevant events. GA4 versus BigQuery discrepancy within normal limits. Every production change needs a documented, tested rollback.

Hard constraint
No production changes during Q4 peak campaigns without explicit client approval. All fixes are validated in staging first.

What we need in your proposal
1. A fixed price for phase one: audit of server-side tracking, audit of GA4 and BigQuery, remediation plan, architecture documentation.
2. A separate estimate for implementing the fixes, once the audit defines them.
3. Your hourly rate for ongoing maintenance and monitoring after go-live, or a monthly retainer.
4. How many working days you need for phase one, assuming access is granted immediately.

How we work
You work inside our accounts, under our agency's name. The client relationship stays with us. We handle all client communication, you handle the technical work. We expect clear written documentation and a non-disclosure and non-circumvention agreement.

Please skip the generic proposal. Tell us about one setup you took over from another vendor, what was broken, and how you proved it was fixed.

Job Title (from earlier): Data Engineer: 100 Independent US Childcare Centers (Florida Only - Strict Filtering & Rules)

Job Description:
I need a clean, highly curated lead list of 100 strictly independent US childcare centers located in Florida only.

Strict Exclusion & Proximity Rules:

No Corporate Chains, Franchises, or Montessori Schools: Corporate chains, franchises, all Montessori schools/programs, faith-based multi-site organizations, school districts, and Head Start programs must be completely excluded.

No Market Competitors / B2B Vendors: Ensure the list contains operating childcare facilities only. Completely exclude any childcare consultants, training agencies, industry associations, software vendors, or local competitor businesses masquerading as centers.

Strict Proximity / Non-Competition Rule: To prevent geographic clustering and ensure we are not targeting competing centers in the same local neighborhood, no two facilities on this list may be located within 3 miles of each other. Every center must be geographically distinct and separated by at least a 3-mile radius from any other center in the dataset.

Note on Urban Density: If you hit a density bottleneck in dense urban areas while enforcing the 3-mile separation rule, cast a wider net across multiple Florida counties (e.g., spreading across Miami-Dade, Broward, Orange, and Hillsborough) rather than crowding a single metro block.

Freelancer Requirements:

Must have fluent English communication and proven experience cleaning and filtering US local business directories or state licensing databases.

Comfortable utilizing tools like Python, Apify, or Clay to automate scraping, state licensing cross-referencing, deduplication, and enrichment.

State & Quota Targets:

Total Volume: Exactly 100 leads from Florida.

Geographic Distribution & Diversity Rules:

Geographic Mix (Approx. 33% each): Urban, Micropolitan, and Rural areas (~33 each).

No Overweight Cities/Metro Areas: To prevent geographic clustering, no single city or local metro area may account for more than 15% (max 15 leads) of the list. The data must feature a wide spread across different cities and counties throughout Florida.

Capacity Brackets (Strictly between 75–175, evenly split at 25% per bracket across the dataset):

Exactly 25 leads: 75–100 capacity

Exactly 25 leads: 101–125 capacity

Exactly 25 leads: 126–150 capacity

Exactly 25 leads: 151–175 capacity

Required Columns:

Facility Name

Decision-Maker Name (Owner, Director, Executive Director, etc.)

Decision-Maker Title

Decision-Maker LinkedIn Profile URL (where available)

Licensed Capacity

Area Type (Urban / Micropolitan / Rural)

City

State

Zip Code

Street Address

Website URL

Project Timeline / Turnaround:

Target Delivery: Completed and delivered within 4 days (96 hours) of awarding the contract.

Deliverable:
Clean CSV or Excel file matching the exact quota, geographic distribution, competitor exclusion, and 3-mile separation rules above.

To Apply:
Please reply with the word "INDEPENDENT", confirm your fluency in English, and briefly explain your experience cleaning US local business databases using Python, Apify, or Clay.

About Ember

Ember is a hospitality hiring platform that helps restaurant workers and employers connect. Workers can showcase their experience and personality, discover restaurants, express interest through our “Spark” feature, and connect with hiring managers.

We’re looking for an experienced freelancer to create short, polished product demo videos that introduce Ember and make its key features easy to understand.

The Project

Our initial project includes three short videos demonstrating how to:

- Spark a restaurant to express interest in working there.
- Connect with a hiring manager.
- Send messages within Ember.

Each video should be approximately 20–45 seconds, with the final length guided by what best communicates the feature. We’ll use these videos for onboarding, our website, and social media.

We want someone who can take time to understand the product, recommend a clear visual approach, and manage production from concept through final delivery.

What You’ll Do

- Collaborate with the founder on messaging, scripts, and storyboards.
- Turn actual Ember screens and workflows into engaging product demonstrations.
- Use motion graphics, interface animations, zooms, and visual highlights to guide viewers through each action.

- Deliver versions optimized for website viewing and vertical social media.
- Provide editable project files so the videos can be updated as the product evolves.

Who We’re Looking For

- A portfolio demonstrating strong experience creating **SaaS product demos, software launch videos, or animated interface walkthroughs**.

- Strong visual storytelling, pacing, typography, and motion design skills.
- Experience working with startups or introducing new software products.
- Attention to detail in accurately representing product functionality.
- Clear communication and the ability to lead the creative process with limited direction.

Experience with marketplaces, recruiting platforms, or consumer-facing apps is a plus. We’re open to your preferred production tools, provided the finished work is polished and easy to maintain.

Deliverables

- Three completed feature demo videos.
- Horizontal and vertical versions of each.
- Captioned exports and editable source files.
- Properly licensed music, fonts, and other third-party assets used in the videos.

We’d like to begin with one paid video to establish the style, then complete the remaining two. There is potential for ongoing work as Ember introduces new features.

ABOUT THE PROJECT

We are a publicly listed AI company building an AI-powered Manufacturing Quality Intelligence & Process Excellence platform for the pharmaceutical industry.

We need a senior freelancer (or a two-person team) to build a working Proof of Concept (PoC) that will be demonstrated to enterprise pharma decision-makers. The end client is confidential.

IMPORTANT:
This is NOT an SAP implementation, SAP HANA migration, ABAP, BASIS, or SAP functional consulting project.

This is primarily a Data Engineering + Data Science + AI application build that uses SAP manufacturing and quality data as input.

SAP knowledge is required only to understand the manufacturing data—not to implement SAP.


WHAT YOU WILL BUILD

A working PoC that analyzes one pharma manufacturing quality process—Batch Review & Release—and answers:

• Where is time being lost?
• What causes rework and delays?
• What should be improved?

Scope includes:

1. Data Pipeline
- Ingest SAP-style CSV/Excel extracts
- Generate realistic synthetic manufacturing event data
- Build a clean event-log model

2. Process Reconstruction (Process Mining)
- Rebuild actual process flows
- Detect variants
- Detect loops
- Identify bottlenecks
- Identify handoffs

3. KPI Analytics Engine
Compute metrics including:
- Batch Release Cycle Time
- Waiting Time
- Processing Time
- Rework %
- Right First Time %
- Handoffs

4. Interactive Dashboards (~7 Screens)
- Process Health Score
- KPI Performance
- Process Flow Visualization
- Site/Product Drilldowns
- Delay Analysis
- Rework Analysis
- Intervention Tracking

5. AI Copilot
Build an LLM-powered assistant that:
- Answers questions about the analytics
- Uses tool/function calling
- Never hallucinates numbers
- Supports scenario analysis

No live SAP integration is required.
The PoC will work entirely from SAP extracts and synthetic data.

About PLENIC Group

PLENIC Group is a Singapore-based advisory and management consultancy working with SMEs and institutions across Southeast Asia. We help our clients grow, transact and operate more efficiently, and practical AI adoption is becoming a core part of that work.

About the Role

We are looking for an Applied AI Workflow Engineer to help businesses turn their everyday processes into practical, reliable AI-powered workflows.

You will work directly with clients to understand how their teams operate, identify suitable opportunities for AI adoption, and implement solutions using platforms such as Claude and
ChatGPT. This includes configuring Projects, Skills, plugins, agents and connectors, and developing custom integrations where out-of-the-box capabilities fall short.

Example use cases include:

• Lead-generation workflows that research prospects, enrich account information and prepare
personalised outreach
• Receipt and invoice processing, including financial data extraction, reconciliation and management reporting
• Talent acquisition support covering candidate screening, interview coordination and stage-based communications
• Internal knowledge assistants that answer questions using company documents and data
• Automation of recurring operational, administrative and reporting tasks

This is a client-facing implementation role. You will move between business process discovery, solution design, hands-on development, testing, deployment and user training.

Engagement Terms
• Location: Remote, open to candidates worldwide
• Basis: Project retainer
• Working hours: Aligned to Singapore time (GMT+8)

Key Responsibilities

Workflow discovery and solution design

• Meet clients and business users to understand their current processes, pain points, systems
and desired outcomes
• Map workflows and identify where AI, automation or better information retrieval can create measurable value
• Translate business requirements into clear technical designs and implementation plans
• Recommend the right platform and architecture based on each client's needs, security requirements and existing technology
• Define where human review, approval and exception handling should sit within each workflow

AI workflow development

• Build and configure Claude Projects, Skills, plugins, connectors and agent-based workflows
• Develop equivalent solutions using ChatGPT Projects, custom GPTs, apps, connectors, agents and other relevant platforms
• Design system instructions, reusable prompts, knowledge structures, tool definitions and multi-step agent workflows
• Build custom integrations using APIs, webhooks and the Model Context Protocol where required
• Connect AI workflows with CRM, email, calendars, cloud storage, accounting software,applicant tracking systems and internal databases
• Implement document ingestion, data extraction, classification, retrieval and structured output
workflows
• Develop lightweight internal applications or interfaces where a conversational interfacealone is insufficient

Testing, governance and deployment

• Create test cases and evaluation datasets to assess accuracy, reliability and consistency
• Identify hallucination, data quality, security and workflow failure risks before deployment
• Implement access controls, audit trails, approval steps and data-handling safeguards
• Monitor deployed workflows and improve them based on usage data and user feedback
• Maintain version control, technical documentation and change records
• Design solutions that the client's own team can maintain and extend

Client enablement

• Run demonstrations, workshops and user acceptance testing with client teams
• Explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical users and decision-makers
• Prepare user guides, administrator guides and workflow documentation
• Train client staff to operate, maintain and progressively improve their solutions
• Support clients through rollout and help drive lasting adoption

What We Are Looking For

• Experience in software engineering, automation, data engineering, solutions engineering or
applied AI
• Hands-on experience building solutions with large language models
• Strong proficiency in Python, JavaScript or TypeScript
• Experience with APIs, webhooks, OAuth, structured data and third-party integrations
• Familiarity with Git, databases and modern cloud-based development
• Ability to design clear prompts, tool instructions, structured outputs and multi-step workflows
• Strong analytical ability and a genuine interest in how businesses actually operate
• Good written and verbal communication skills
• Confidence working directly with clients and facilitating discussions with business users
• Ability to manage several client workstreams and own them from discovery through
deployment
• A practical, experimental mindset with strong attention to detail

Preferred Experience

Experience in any of the following would be an advantage:

• Claude, Claude Code, the Anthropic API, Claude Projects, Skills or connectors
• ChatGPT, Codex, the OpenAI API, custom GPTs, apps or agent-based workflows
• Model Context Protocol servers and custom tool integrations
• Workflow platforms such as n8n, Make, Zapier or Power Automate
• Retrieval-augmented generation, vector databases and enterprise knowledge assistants
• LLM evaluation, monitoring and guardrail frameworks
• OCR, document intelligence and financial document processing
• CRM, accounting, HR, recruitment or applicant tracking systems
• AWS, Azure or Google Cloud
• Cybersecurity, data privacy and enterprise AI governance

You Will Do Well Here If You

• Are curious about both technology and business operations
• Can turn an ambiguous business problem into a structured implementation plan

Author Assistant and Content Lead

Eve Saint Laurent Press · Remote · Freelance, long term

Calling every witchy dark romance reader

Eve Saint Laurent Press is a small independent imprint about to launch the first book in a seven-book gothic dark romance series.

It's sexy, sharp, funny and a little dangerous. There's an ambitious heroine, a world-famous actor who's probably a terrible idea, a gothic mansion and a dead ex who won't stay quiet. Underneath all that, a woman is waking up to her own power, and to knowledge the world taught women to fear.

Book one publishes on Amazon on 24 November 2026. We're looking for the person who'll help the right readers find it, fall for it and never shut up about it. Once we've talked, we'll share much more about the book and the series.

The world you'll be creating for

Our content lives in seven themes, each with its own look, tone and audience:

1. Our heroine: awakening, power and becoming. Her ambition, intuition, sexuality and growing power.
2. The witchy and metaphysical. Signs, synchronicity, dreams, manifestation, and the feeling that reality is bigger than it looks.
3. Dark romance and erotic tension. Desire, danger, obsession and a very complicated man.
4. Haunting, past lives and secrets. The mansion, the dead ex, and a connection that may be centuries old.
5. The feminist call. Women reclaiming their power and refusing to make themselves smaller.
6. The serpent and reclaimed knowledge. Forbidden wisdom, and who decided it was forbidden.
7. The author's voice. Why she wrote it, and what makes it different.

The tone is witty, knowing, a bit feral and never preachy. If you already talk like this in your own feed, you'll feel right at home.

The role

This is a long-term place on the team. You'll help launch book one, then grow with us across all seven books. You'll work closely with the author and our commercial lead, supported by AI tools we use for research and first drafts. You bring the creative instinct, the genre knowledge and a feel for what our readers will love.

You'll get the inside track from day one. You'll read the manuscript before anyone else, and you'll get the full content bible: ready-made copy, a library of video clips and hashtag sets for every theme. Then you'll have real freedom to bring your own ideas, try new formats and tell us what's working.

What you'll do

Lead the content (the heart of the job)

- Turn the seven themes into a steady stream of reels, carousels, quote cards and stories that stop the scroll.
- Pair the right clip with the right line and the right hashtags, and keep a good mix of themes across the week.
- Write fresh captions and hooks in the same voice: funny, sexy, knowing, never preachy.
- Run TikTok, Instagram and Facebook, and help us grow into X, Threads, Pinterest, YouTube Shorts or wherever our readers are.
- Plan and schedule a week at a time, see what lands, and make more of it.
- Grow the community: reply to comments, spark debates, run polls and theory prompts, and share fan content.

Get the book into readers' hands

- Recruit and look after a team of ARC readers who'll love this book, and encourage honest reviews on Amazon and Goodreads.
- Find Bookstagram and BookTok creators who suit the series and get them excited about it.
- Rally a street team for launch day.

Keep us on track

- Keep the content calendar and trackers current, and share a quick weekly look at the numbers.
- Work alongside our AI tools. Use them to research and draft faster, and give them your creative direction.

You'll be perfect for this if

- You are our reader. Dark romance is on your shelf, and there might be a tarot deck on your bedside table.
- You've helped launch indie romance books before, and you can show us what you did and how it went.
- You're a content creator at heart. You know the trends, formats and hashtags on BookTok and Bookstagram, and you're curious about new platforms.
- Your written English is excellent: fluent, natural and full of personality.
- You're fluent in modern tools. You know your way around design, video, scheduling and AI tools, and you're always picking up whatever helps you create faster and better.
- You're organised enough to hit deadlines without being chased.
- You can keep a secret. You'll know things long before readers do.
- You want to be part of something from the start and grow with it.

Bonus points

- You bring an ARC team, street team or network of bookish creators.
- You have your own bookish following.
- You've run Amazon or Meta ads for books.
- Witchcraft, shadow work, astrology or past lives are your thing too.

The practical bits

Where: Remote, from anywhere
Type: Freelance, long term
Hours: Flexible, busiest October to December
Start: October 2026
Terms: We'll agree them together

How to apply

Experienced candidates only, please. This role is for someone who has already done this job for authors. Apply only if you can show us real work we can check. Applications without links to verifiable work won't be considered.

Start your application by telling us the last dark romance you couldn't put down. That's how we'll know you've read this far.

Then include:

1. Links to one or two book launches you've worked on: the book, what you did and the results.
2. Links to social accounts you've run or created content for.
3. A reference from an author you've worked with.
4. Three captions with hashtags, for any of our seven themes. Show us your voice.
5. When you could start.

We'll start with a relaxed video call. Then there's a short paid trial task and a chat with the author. We'd love to have someone on board by mid-October.
Client's questions:

  • Share links to social accounts you've run or created content for.
  • Which platforms and tools, including AI tools, do you use day to day to create and schedule content?
  • When could you start, and how many hours a week can you give from October to December?

I’m looking for an experienced full-stack developer with strong data architecture experience to build the first commercial version of a new B2B data intelligence SaaS platform.

This is not a basic website or simple dashboard. The product will organize and continuously update large amounts of business and location data, identify relationships between entities, and make that intelligence searchable through a modern, intuitive SaaS interface.

The initial project is a commercially usable V1, but I’m looking for someone who can build the right foundation for a much more sophisticated platform over time. For the right developer, this could become a significant ongoing development opportunity.

Core V1 Requirements

The platform will need to:

Import and manage structured and semi-structured data, including CSV and document-derived data
Normalize, clean and deduplicate business records
Connect companies, legal entities, brands, locations, people and related records
Support entity resolution, fuzzy matching and identification of potentially related entities
Provide an internal review process for uncertain matches
Maintain source/provenance information and support ongoing data updates
Provide fast search, filtering and detailed profiles
Allow users to save/manage lists or watchlists
Present interconnected data through a clean, professional B2B interface
Multi-Tenant SaaS

This needs to be built as a true multi-tenant SaaS platform.

Each customer organization may have multiple users, including an organization admin and standard users. Customer accounts and data must be appropriately separated.

Our internal team will need platform-level/super-admin capabilities to manage customers, users, records, entity relationships, data quality and other platform functions.

The architecture should also accommodate future subscription tiers and feature-based permissions.

Data & AI

The underlying dataset will continually evolve as new information becomes available. The platform therefore needs to be designed for ongoing ingestion, updating and data cleansing, rather than as a static database.

We also expect to use AI/LLMs strategically for areas such as document/data extraction, classification, cleansing, entity matching and processing new information.

V1 does not need to automate every future data workflow. I would rather build a strong foundation with automated matching/confidence scoring plus human review where appropriate, and increase automation over time.

Ideal Background

I’m particularly interested in experience with:

Full-stack SaaS development
Python
PostgreSQL and relational database architecture
React / Next.js
Data engineering / ETL
Database Development
API development
Entity resolution / record linkage / fuzzy matching
AI/LLM-assisted data processing
Multi-tenant SaaS architecture
Authentication and role-based permissions
Search and data-heavy applications
Cloud deployment

I’m open to alternative technology recommendations if you can explain why they are better suited to the product.

How I’d Like to Work

I’m looking for someone who can think through the product with me, not simply code from a rigid specification.

I understand the business problem and what I want the product to accomplish, but I want the developer to help translate that into the right technical architecture, identify potential issues early, and recommend what should be included in V1 versus deferred.

Good communication is important. I’d like regular progress updates and working builds throughout development rather than waiting until the end of the project to see the product.

The initial engagement will be milestone-based, with the potential to transition into ongoing development work as the platform grows.

When Applying

Please include examples of data-heavy SaaS applications you personally built, particularly anything involving large datasets, entity matching, search, multi-tenant accounts or AI-assisted data processing.

Also briefly answer:

What technology stack would you recommend and why?
Have you built multi-tenant SaaS applications with organization admins and multiple users?
Have you worked with entity resolution, fuzzy matching or deduplication?
How would you approach a V1 so it is cost-effective now but can scale later?
Which portions of the project would you personally handle?

Please do not send only generic website, WordPress, Shopify or e-commerce examples. I’m specifically looking for someone with experience building data-centric software products.

Additional information about the specific industry, data sources and business model will be shared with shortlisted candidates.

Developer Takeover & Completion of Phases 2–4

Fixed-price project: $500

Potential long-term collaboration after completion

About the project

PROVUS Site Intelligence™ is an industrial field-intelligence platform being developed for complex industrial environments such as tank terminals, chemical plants and refineries.

The platform connects physical field evidence with engineering information such as:

* P&IDs;
* equipment and tag numbers;
* field photographs;
* GPS and spatial information;
* work orders;
* IBM Maximo data;
* engineering documents;
* findings and verification history.

A substantial part of the platform has already been developed.

Our current developer will provide a full technical handover to the selected new developer.

We are therefore not looking for someone to rebuild the application from scratch.

We are looking for a hands-on developer who can take ownership of the existing system, understand what has already been built, complete the remaining agreed Phase 2–4 functionality and bring the platform to the point where we can start testing it with real industrial customers.

⸻

Current status

The existing platform already includes a substantial technical foundation, including:

* Android field application;
* web dashboard;
* backend/API;
* database;
* field photo capture and upload;
* GPS capture;
* evidence and findings;
* initial computer vision;
* OCR/tag recognition;
* P&ID Field Check functionality;
* detection/evidence review;
* before/after verification;
* verification routes;
* Site Intelligence functionality;
* Value Ledger foundation;
* annotation/training environment;
* existing labelled industrial image data;
* initial model research and testing.

The outgoing developer has also completed additional development after the original MVP.

The first responsibility of the new developer is therefore to understand and verify the actual current state before continuing development.

⸻

IMPORTANT — THIS IS A CONTINUATION PROJECT

The total fixed budget of:

USD 500

covers:

1. Takeover of the existing system
2. Verification of the current implementation
3. Completion of the remaining Phase 2 work
4. Completion of Phase 3
5. Completion of Phase 4
6. End-to-end preparation for customer pilots

The takeover is not a separate $500 assignment.

The complete continuation scope described below is included in the $500 total fixed price.

⸻

MILESTONE 1

Takeover + Verification + Remaining Phase 2

$200

1. Technical takeover

The outgoing developer will provide a structured handover.

The new developer must take ownership of and verify all relevant existing technical assets, including:

* source-code repositories;
* backend;
* dashboard;
* Android application;
* database;
* deployment/environment;
* object/file storage;
* AI/vision services;
* document-processing services;
* annotation environment;
* existing datasets;
* existing annotations;
* model files;
* training configurations;
* benchmark/evaluation results;
* relevant technical documentation.

The objective is not simply to receive files.

The new developer must be able to independently run and continue the existing system.

Any missing handover information should be identified immediately so it can still be requested from the outgoing developer.

⸻

2. Preserve existing functionality

Existing working functionality must not be unnecessarily rebuilt.

The new developer should first establish:

WORKING

Already functional and should be preserved.

PARTIALLY COMPLETE

Exists but requires further development.

NOT COMPLETE

Still needs to be implemented.

BLOCKED

Cannot currently be completed because customer access/data/API credentials or another external dependency is required.

This should be done quickly as part of the takeover, not as a lengthy separate discovery project.

⸻

3. Existing dataset and annotations

A significant amount of industrial annotation work has already been completed.

This work must be preserved.

The developer must verify and take over:

* original training images;
* existing annotations;
* class definitions;
* class IDs;
* human corrections;
* Label Studio data;
* dataset exports;
* train/validation/test splits where available;
* model checkpoints;
* existing benchmark results.

Do not restart annotation from zero unless technically justified.

⸻

4. Industrial computer vision

Continue the existing computer-vision work.

The main direction is not simply generic defect detection.

The objective is to understand:

What equipment/component is visible, what is its physical state, where is it located and how does this relate to the engineering information?

Relevant classes/conditions already investigated include items such as:

* pipe ends/connections;
* blind flanges;
* quick couplings;
* insulation;
* guards;
* temporary/flexible connections;
* industrial equipment/components.

The preferred architecture is:

detect/localise component

→

assess visible condition

→

human review where required

The system must support uncertainty rather than forcing a false conclusion.

⸻

5. Human review

Existing review functionality should continue to support:

* Accept;
* Correct;
* Reject;
* Uncertain / additional evidence required.

Store, where relevant:

* original prediction;
* model/version;
* confidence;
* engineer decision;
* corrected result;
* evidence reference;
* reviewer;
* timestamp.

These reviewed results should later feed the Phase 4 learning workflow.

⸻

6. Field capture quality

Complete/improve the Android capture workflow so that the field user can receive quick feedback before leaving the equipment location.

Where technically feasible, check for:

* blurred image;
* unreadable tag;
* insufficient image quality;
* target not sufficiently visible;
* required perspective missing;
* additional photograph required.

The purpose is simple:

Do not discover after leaving the field that the required evidence is unusable.

⸻

7. Spatial capture data

Field captures should use/store available information such as:

* GPS;
* GPS accuracy;
* timestamp;
* compass/heading;
* device orientation;
* asset/task relationship;
* capture sequence.

This information will be used to connect field evidence with the site and engineering context.

⸻

8. Connected photographs / image stitching

Continue the feasibility work for recognising photographs that belong to the same physical environment.

Example:

A user takes photograph A.

The next photograph is taken slightly to the right and contains approximately 30% overlap.

PROVUS should investigate whether these images can be automatically related using combinations of:

* visual overlap;
* feature matching;
* GPS;
* compass direction;
* timestamps;
* capture sequence;
* detected equipment;
* detected tags.

The user should not need to install physical reference markers.

A production-grade Google Street View or full 3D reconstruction is not required within this milestone.

The objective is a practical method that can be used within the PROVUS workflow.

⸻

Milestone 1 acceptance

Milestone 1 is complete when:

* the new developer can independently run the existing platform;
* relevant existing data/models/annotations have been secured;
* the current technical state is clear;
* existing functionality remains operational;
* the remaining Phase 2 vision workflow is functioning at the agreed practical level;
* capture-quality improvements are integrated;
* relevant location/orientation data is captured;
* connected-photo feasibility can be demonstrated.

Milestone 1: $200

⸻

MILESTONE 2

Complete Phase 3 — Connected Site Intelligence

$300

This is the largest continuation milestone.

The objective is to connect:

FIELD REALITY ↔ ASSET ↔ LOCATION ↔ P&ID ↔ ENGINEERING DATA

⸻

9. P&ID intelligence

P&IDs are central to PROVUS Site Intelligence.

The existing P&ID Field Check functionality should be extended into a structured P&ID information layer.

The system should, where technically applicable:

* upload P&IDs;
* extract/read text and tags;
* OCR drawings where required;
* index tag numbers;
* store drawing/revision metadata;
* connect tags to relevant assets;
* make P&IDs searchable;
* avoid unnecessarily processing an entire drawing repeatedly through an LLM.

Ultimately, a user should be able to open a P&ID and use the equipment/tag information as an entry point into the available plant information.

⸻

10. Asset knowledge

Selecting an equipment tag should expose the information PROVUS has connected to that equipment.

For example:

P-101B

could show:

* field photographs;
* latest verified state;
* P&IDs;
* findings;
* work orders;
* maintenance information;
* MOCs;
* inspection information;
* datasheets;
* project files;
* relevant history.

The exact available information depends on the customer’s data.

⸻

11. Document intelligence

PROVUS should read relevant document contents, not only filenames.

Continue/improve ingestion of relevant supported information such as:

* PDFs;
* P&IDs;
* Excel/CSV files;
* equipment lists;
* instrument lists;
* line lists;
* MOC information;
* inspection reports;
* datasheets;
* project documentation.

The information should become searchable and connectable to relevant tags/assets where possible.

⸻

12. Field photograph ↔ P&ID ↔ location

This is one of the most important parts of the system.

The field workflow should progressively connect:

* photograph;
* detected/selected tag;
* equipment;
* GPS;
* compass direction;
* surrounding equipment;
* P&ID;
* plot plan;
* aerial imagery;
* related documents.

For example, when a field photograph contains tanks 815 and 816 and recognisable surrounding structures, the system should use the available field and spatial information to help determine where the photograph was taken and in which direction the camera was facing.

The objective is to relate the physical photograph to its position on the site.

The source requirements explicitly expect the aerial image, photograph and GPS position to be matched and represented against the plot plan. Site-Intelligence expectation (1).docx

⸻

13. Physical field state vs P&ID

PROVUS should support identifying possible differences between the physical plant and engineering information.

Example:

A previous state/P&ID shows a three-way valve.

Current field evidence appears to show that the valve has been removed and replaced by a spool piece.

The system should not blindly declare an engineering conclusion.

It should be able to flag something such as:

POSSIBLE FIELD / P&ID MISMATCH

and recommend investigation, for example:

Check whether equipment is temporarily removed for maintenance or permanently changed through an MOC/project.

Where evidence is insufficient, the system should request additional close/far photographs rather than force a conclusion. This behaviour is specifically contemplated in the supplied functional expectations. Site-Intelligence expectation (1).docx

⸻

14. Plot plan + PDOK

Complete the site-map functionality.

For Dutch sites this should include, where technically suitable:

Plot plan view

Customer-provided site plot plan.

Aerial view

High-resolution PDOK aerial imagery.

The user should be able to:

* zoom;
* navigate the site;
* switch between relevant views;
* return to the site centre;
* view relevant evidence/assets/findings;
* relate field evidence to the site.

Where possible, use the appropriate high-resolution PDOK imagery and support the required site context. The supplied Phase 3 requirements specifically call for switchable plot-plan and PDOK aerial views. Site-intelligence new functionalities.docx

⸻

15. Customer/site access

Normal customer users should only access the site(s) assigned to them.

A customer user should not simply be able to switch into another customer’s environment.

PROVUS administrators may have cross-site access for:

* support;
* configuration;
* quality control.

⸻

16. Dashboard home

Create/complete a useful landing page instead of dropping the customer directly into the map.

The customer should immediately understand relevant information such as:

* current site;
* verification priorities;
* open findings;
* outstanding field work;
* evidence requiring review;
* relevant assets/areas;
* Value Ledger summary where available.

⸻

17. Microsoft login

Implement/complete Microsoft enterprise authentication where technically suitable.

Prefer Microsoft Entra ID/Azure AD with the appropriate role/site relationship.

⸻

18. IBM Maximo integration

Complete the IBM Maximo integration.

This is not described as a “basic” integration.

The exact implementation method may be selected by the developer based on what is technically appropriate and what access is available.

Relevant Maximo functionality should support the agreed workflow around:

* tag numbers;
* assets;
* work orders;
* maintenance/inspection information;
* P&ID references;
* functional locations;
* relevant PROVUS evidence/findings.

For example:

If the physical tag differs from the Maximo tag, PROVUS may search reasonable alternatives but the inconsistency itself should remain visible.

If a tag exists in Maximo, relevant maintenance/inspection information and engineering references should be available for comparison where the API/data permits.

If a tag exists in Maximo but not on the P&ID, this can become an inconsistency requiring review.

These are explicitly part of the supplied Maximo requirements. Site-intelligence new functionalities.docx

Where the available customer/API environment permits, relevant information should also be capable of being transferred back toward Maximo.

Do not tightly couple the complete PROVUS architecture to Maximo. The integration approach should allow later connections to other EAM systems.

⸻

Milestone 2 acceptance

Milestone 2 is complete when the agreed Phase 3 workflow can be demonstrated, including:

* P&ID/tag indexing;
* connected asset context;
* relevant document-content retrieval;
* field evidence connected to asset/P&ID context;
* spatial/site context;
* plot-plan/PDOK functionality;
* appropriate site/user access;
* dashboard landing page;
* agreed Microsoft authentication;
* agreed Maximo functionality within the available environment.

Milestone 2: $300

⸻

MILESTONE 3

Complete Phase 4 + Pilot Readiness

$250

The objective of Phase 4 is to close the loop.

PROVUS should not only detect and store information.

Verified field activity should progressively improve the system.

⸻

19. Closed learning loop

Complete the workflow:

system/model prediction

→

human Accept / Correct / Reject / Uncertain

→

validated result

→

training candidate

→

dataset

→

retraining

→

evaluation

→

approved new model

The process should be practical and repeatable.

A large enterprise MLOps platform is not required at this stage.

⸻

20. Model and dataset traceability

Maintain practical traceability for:

* dataset version;
* model version;
* training run;
* evaluation result;
* deployment status;
* human correction.

For a relevant detection, we should be able to determine which model/version generated it.

⸻

21. Active learning

Where practical, prioritise useful examples for future review/training.

Examples:

* low confidence;
* uncertain result;
* human correction;
* repeated error;
* novel condition;
* disagreement.

The objective is to make future human review useful for improving PROVUS rather than simply creating more manual work.

⸻

22. PlantSync improvement

Use the growing body of evidence to improve verification priorities.

Relevant factors may include:

* evidence age;
* recent work;
* modifications;
* missing evidence;
* open findings;
* conflicting records;
* previous verification results;
* relevant asset/site context.

The reason behind a priority should remain explainable.

⸻

23. Site Intelligence

Complete/improve the contextual intelligence workflow so the system can combine available:

* field evidence;
* P&IDs;
* assets;
* documents;
* findings;
* verification results;
* Maximo information;
* human corrections.

Site Intelligence should remain evidence-grounded.

If sufficient evidence is not available, it should say so.

⸻

24. Value Ledger

Complete the practical Value Event workflow.

Relevant events should be capable of linking:

* event;
* evidence;
* baseline;
* actual result;
* agreed customer parameter/value;
* calculation;
* approval state.

Maintain distinction between:

* measured value;
* modelled value;
* approved value;
* risk intervention.

The system should not automatically claim financial value simply because an AI detection occurred.

⸻

25. End-to-end pilot workflow

Before final acceptance, demonstrate one complete workflow through the system.

For example:

P&ID / asset

→ PlantSync verification priority

→ field mission

→ Android navigation/context

→ field photographs

→ capture-quality check

→ GPS/heading/context

→ OCR/component assessment

→ connected field evidence

→ P&ID comparison

→ possible finding

→ human review

→ asset knowledge updated

→ Site Intelligence

→ Value Event

→ reviewed result retained for future learning.

The purpose is to demonstrate that PROVUS operates as one connected product, rather than a collection of separate prototype functions.

⸻

26. Pilot-ready handover

At the end of the project:

* code must be committed to PROVUS-controlled repositories;
* relevant configuration must be documented;
* database changes/migrations must be included;
* deployment instructions must be current;
* relevant model/dataset information must be available;
* known limitations must be documented;
* the platform must be ready for the next stage: real customer pilots.

⸻

Milestone 3 acceptance

Phase 4 is accepted when:

* the feedback/training loop is demonstrable;
* model/dataset traceability works at the agreed practical level;
* PlantSync uses the improved evidence context;
* Site Intelligence uses the connected information;
* Value Event logic functions;
* one complete pilot workflow has been demonstrated;
* the system can be continued without dependency on the outgoing developer.

Milestone 3: $250

⸻

SMALL CHANGES DURING DEVELOPMENT

This is important.

Because this is an existing product moving toward customer pilots, we expect that small, incidental changes, refinements and additions may arise during implementation, integration and testing.

These are expected to be included within the agreed $500 fixed price where they reasonably belong to the existing Phase 2–4 scope.

Examples could include:

* adding a small field;
* changing a label/status;
* minor UI adjustment;
* small workflow refinement;
* minor API adjustment;
* small database adjustment;
* additional validation;
* small change required to make an agreed feature work properly;
* minor improvement identified during testing.

We do not want every small adjustment to become a new commercial discussion.

However, a materially new module, major integration or substantial new requirement that clearly falls outside the Phase 2–4 scope will be discussed separately before development begins.

⸻

BUDGET & MILESTONES

Milestone Fixed price
1. Takeover + Verification + Remaining Phase 2 $200
2. Complete Phase 3 — Connected Site Intelligence $300
3. Complete Phase 4 + Pilot Readiness $250
TOTAL FIXED PRICE $500

Payment is released after completion and acceptance of each milestone.

⸻

WHAT HAPPENS AFTER THIS PROJECT?

This project does not represent the end of PROVUS development.

It represents the transition from product development into:

REAL CUSTOMER PILOTS

After Phase 4 we intend to take the platform into industrial customer environments and test it with actual:

* field engineers;
* plant equipment;
* customer P&IDs;
* customer documents;
* customer asset data;
* Maximo environments;
* site workflows;
* industrial photographs.

Those pilots will naturally create further development work.

This may include:

* customer-specific integrations;
* new equipment/classes;
* additional training data;
* model improvements;
* false-positive/false-negative improvements;
* field-app improvements;
* customer-specific workflows;
* deployment work;
* security improvements;
* additional EAM integrations;
* dashboard improvements;
* Value Ledger configuration;
* new functionality arising from real field use.

We therefore see this takeover as the start of a potential long-term development relationship, not a one-off $500 project.

We expect ongoing product and pilot development to continue for at least approximately the following 12 months, subject to successful collaboration, technical performance and actual customer requirements.

Future customer-pilot work is not included in the present $500 budget and will be contracted separately as new work arises.

⸻

OWNERSHIP & HANDOVER

All work must be performed in or transferred to PROVUS-controlled environments.

PROVUS must retain access to all relevant:

* source code;
* repositories;
* database structures/migrations;
* deployment files;
* model files created for the project;
* PROVUS-specific training configuration;
* annotations/datasets created for the project;
* documentation.

The developer should not create a technical dependency that prevents another qualified developer from continuing the system later.

⸻

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for someone who is comfortable taking responsibility for an existing product, rather than only building isolated features.

Relevant experience includes:

* Python / FastAPI;
* computer vision;
* YOLO or comparable vision models;
* OCR;
* model training/fine-tuning;
* PostgreSQL;
* PostGIS;
* vector search/pgvector;
* React/TypeScript;
* Android/Kotlin;
* Docker;
* APIs/integrations;
* geospatial data;
* document processing/RAG;
* industrial/engineering information systems.

Experience with:

* P&IDs;
* industrial assets;
* IBM Maximo;
* industrial computer vision;
* spatial field evidence

is a strong advantage.

⸻

WHEN APPLYING

Please answer briefly:

1. Have you previously taken over an existing codebase from another developer?

Explain one relevant example.

2. Which parts of this stack can you personally work on?

Python/FastAPI, React, Android/Kotlin, computer vision/model training, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, document processing, integrations.

3. How would you approach the first 2–3 days of this takeover?

We are specifically interested in how you would verify the existing application before changing it.

4. Have you worked with computer vision where human corrections become future training data?

If yes, briefly explain.

5. Do you have experience with P&IDs, Maximo, industrial assets or similar engineering systems?

Not mandatory, but relevant.

6. When can you start and how much availability do you have over the coming weeks?

⸻

Final objective

At the end of this $500 project we do not expect a completely different application.

We expect the existing PROVUS platform to have been successfully taken over, completed through the remaining Phase 2–4 scope and brought to a state where we can begin:

REAL CUSTOMER PILOTS.

That is the finish line for this assignment.

Project Scope
You will design and build a complete management dashboard that may include:
- Incoming and outgoing calls
- Call performance and conversion metrics
- Customer check-ins

Search Query Syntax Instructions

When multiple keywords are entered, for example logo, design, website, the search engine finds projects containing any of these words in the title, description, or skills. To customize the search scope, use the checkboxes under 'Advanced Keywords Options' to enable/disable searching within title, description, or skills fields.

All Keywords Search

To find projects that contain all of your keywords, use the AND operator between words:

  • logo AND design AND website - Must include all three words
  • react AND developer - Must include both "react" and "developer"

Wildcards

Use * to match variations of a word:

  • develop* - Matches "developer", "development", "developing", etc.

Exact Phrases

Use quotes for exact phrase matches:

  • "website design" - Finds the exact phrase "website design"

Must-Include Terms

Use the + symbol before any word that must be present. For example:

  • +website +design logo - Must include both "website" and "design", "logo" is optional

Excluded Terms

Use the - symbol to exclude specific terms. For example:

  • +developer -wordpress - Must include "developer" but exclude projects with "wordpress"

Advanced Search Mode provides the same functionality as Basic Search, but uses a text field instead of tags for greater control and visibility. This makes it easier to:

  • Write and edit complex queries
  • See your entire search at once
  • Copy and save queries for later use
  • Fine-tune your search terms

All instructions from Basic Search work in Advanced Mode:

  • AND operator: logo AND design AND website
  • Must-include (+): +website +design logo
  • Exclude (-): +developer -wordpress
  • Wildcards (*): develop*
  • Exact phrases: "website design"

Default Search Behavior

By default, all terms are optional. By entering app design mobile you'll find projects that contain any of these words.

More Advanced Operators

Advanced Mode adds these powerful features:

Search by Field

You can search within specific fields using field prefixes:

Available fields:

  • title: - Search in project titles
  • description: - Search in project descriptions
  • skills: - Search in required skills

Examples:

  • title:wordpress AND skills:php - Find WordPress in projects title and PHP in Skills
  • description:"mobile app" AND NOT skills:flutter - Find "mobile app" in projects descriptions and Skills doesn't contains Flutter
  • skills:(react OR vue) AND title:frontend - Find frontend in projects title and Skills contains React or Vue

Boolean Operators

You can use AND, OR, NOT for complex queries:

Examples:

  • mobile OR web
  • ui AND design NOT wordpress

Grouping Terms

Use parentheses to group terms and create sub-queries:

Examples:

  • (frontend OR backend) AND (react OR node)
  • (UI OR UX) AND mobile AND NOT (wordpress OR shopify)

Pro Tips

  • Always use parentheses when combining different operators
  • You can mix basic and advanced syntax: +react (vue OR angular)
  • Group similar alternatives within parentheses
  • Start simple and add complexity as needed

Understand how 'Freelancer Location' works

US/UK-based special feeds

There is a specific U.S. feed available to US-based freelancers only and a specific U.K. feed available to UK-based freelancers only.

Clients in the USA (only) can restrict their job posts to be visible to freelancers in the USA only, and clients in the UK (only) can restrict their job posts to freelancers in the UK only.

We added filter attributes to manage how to display projects from these special feeds. Now you can include (by default), exclude, or show only projects from these feeds.

Freelancer Location

Clients from any country can set a location preference to any country. This doesn't mean that only freelancers from that country will see the projects, but it means that client might give priority to freelancers from that country.

We added filter attributes for better control over this behavior.

When you select a country in 'Freelancer Location' filter, it will show only projects where client has set this country as Location in Preferred qualifications, and hide all other projects where it's not set. Use 'Include projects without preferred freelancer location' to also show jobs without any Location qualifications. If no Freelancer Location is selected, this option does not narrow the results.

Filter by lower range value

Some Upwork jobs post a budget range instead of one figure — an hourly job at $30–$80/hr, say, or a fixed-price job with a low and high estimate. This setting decides which end of that range your minimum budget has to meet.

Off (default) — match either end

A job shows if either end of its range meets your minimum, so a range that starts below your minimum but reaches above it still gets through.

On — match the lower end

A job shows only if the lower end meets your minimum, which drops jobs that reach it only at the top of their range.

Example

Say your minimum hourly rate is $50/hr:

Job posted at Off (default) On
$30–$80/hr Shown ($80 ≥ $50) Hidden ($30 < $50)
$60–$120/hr Shown ($60 ≥ $50) Shown ($60 ≥ $50)

Works the same for hourly and fixed-price ranges. With no minimum budget set, it has no effect.

Include clients without sufficient history

Upwork only reports a client's spend, hires, rating, and reviews once that client has run some contracts. Brand-new clients have no track record yet — Vollna treats them as having no sufficient history. This setting decides whether those clients still reach you once you've set client-quality filters.

On (default) — keep no-history clients

A client with no track record is shown even when you've set a minimum Total spend, Hires, Rating, or Reviews. Those thresholds are skipped for them, because there's no data to check against — so a brand-new client can appear alongside your minimum-spend results.

Off — require enough history

A client must have enough history to be judged. Anyone Upwork reports no data for is hidden, so only clients whose figures meet your thresholds get through.

This only affects clients with missing data. A client with a recorded spend below your minimum is always hidden — whether this is on or off.

Example

Say your minimum Total spend is $1,000:

Client On (default) Off
New client, no history Shown (no data to check) Hidden
Spent $400 Hidden ($400 < $1,000) Hidden ($400 < $1,000)
Spent $5,000 Shown ($5,000 ≥ $1,000) Shown ($5,000 ≥ $1,000)

Applies to every client-history filter — Total spend, Hires, Rating, Reviews, and more. With no client filters set, it has no effect.

Switch to Basic search?

Your advanced query uses operators (like AND or grouping) that can’t be shown as keyword tags. In Basic, the filter will search by your tags instead of this query. The query isn’t deleted — switch back to Advanced any time to use it again.

Keywords and query don’t match

Your keyword tags and the advanced search query are different. Choose which one this filter should use — the other will be replaced.
